messages:
ananya: hey team — bringing up a HF checkpoint (gpt-neox-20b-variant) in the redwood conversion flow. After convert -> quantize -> serve we saw weird token id desyncs for special tokens (bos/eos/pad). The model was fine in HF testing but in Redwood outputs the first token is an unexpected token id.

ananya: minimal repro: tokenizer in HF has added_tokens.json with entries like:
```json
[ {"id":50256,"content":"<|bos|>"}, {"id":50257,"content":"<|eos|>"} ]
```
but after our conversion the tokenizer.vocab reports different ids (50256 now points to '<|unk|>').

laura: hmm. did you pass the original tokenizer files (vocab.json merges or tokenizer.json) straight into the conversion script or did you rebuild from added_tokens?

ananya: passed the HF repo dir into convert_tool.py. It emitted a redwood tokenizer bundle. I compared tokenizer.get_vocab() pre/post and many ids shifted by +1 or so. It looks like added_tokens were appended in a different order during the conversion.

charlie: common pitfall: HF "added_tokens.json" is just a list and the converters sometimes reindex when writing a new vocab file (especially for byte-level BPE tokenizers). The converter we use currently reserializes the vocab and doesn't preserve explicit ids in added_tokens.json.

mike: also check config.json for bos_token_id/eos_token_id/pad_token_id — if those are absent converter may fallback to heuristics. If bos_token_id is missing, redwood runtime may set a default.

ananya: config.json did have bos_token as "<|bos|>" but bos_token_id was null. I assumed the id would be inferred. Apparently inference path expects explicit ids for the private deploy.

charlie: quick diagnostics we use: 1) dump tokenizer.get_vocab() from HF before convert 2) dump vocab file after convert 3) run a small script mapping token -> id and compare diffs. Example:
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('path/to/hf')
print({k:v for k,v in sorted(t.get_vocab().items(), key=lambda x:x[1])[:20]})
```
That will show if special tokens moved.

laura: workaround until converter change: re-run tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'bos_token':'<|bos|>','eos_token':'<|eos|>','pad_token':'<|pad|>'}) on the converted tokenizer and then set tokenizer.bos_token_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|bos|>') explicitly, then save_pretrained. That forces consistent ids in the saved tokenizer bundle.

mike: note re quantization: some quant pipelines (we use 8-bit Q) create a compacted embedding table and in our conversion code we were accidentally remapping embedding indices to a contiguous range THEN writing special token ids based on the old indexes. So embeddings and token ids diverged. The fix is to remap special token ids after compaction, not before.

ananya: interesting — that would explain why HF eval (without quant) looked ok but quantized runtime shows crashy outputs. I can repro: unquantized convert = OK, quantize step = breaks ids.

charlie: action: I'll open a small PR to the conversion lib to 1) preserve explicit ids when present, 2) after any embedding compaction pass, re-assign special token ids by looking up token strings. There's also an edge-case where added_tokens have multiple string forms.

laura: also add an automated check in onboarding CI: after conversion assert tokenizer.decode([bos_token_id]) == '<|bos|>' and same for eos/pad. Fail early.

ananya: doing that now. quick test locally:
```bash
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('conv/tokenizer.json'); print(t.token_to_id('<|bos|>'))"
```
returns None on the broken artifact.

mike: when you file the issue/PR, include the quant pipeline trace and the small diff of vocab files. I suspect this will also fix a customer-facing regression we saw in Dedicated earlier this week.

deploy-bot: build 4207 finished — artifact: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4207/converter/ (includes conversion-lib tests) :package:
